To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a visuomotor training program that involves the whole body in the teaching of letters, is more effective than a visual training program, at least for letter recognition.

1) a teacher-implemented whole body visuotactile intervention is effective in teaching cursive letter recognition in 5-year-olds, and 2) the visuomotion program has mixed effects on letter handwriting, with higher scores on stroke quality but lower scores on handwriting fluency, compared with a visual training program.
visuomotor training in kindergarten is more effective than a visual training program for letter recognition and letter writing, but not for fluency of handwriting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the motor system in children with cerebral palsy.
the role of visuomotor experience in learning to write letters.
the development of letter knowledge, which is a fundamental skill for reading and writing, and a key indicator of children’s academic progress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a visuomotor program is more effective than a visual program for letter recognition, but not for letter production.
visuomotor interventions can be effective in improving children’s letter knowledge.
visuomotor interventions are more effective than visual ones in teaching letter recognition, but not necessarily for letter handwriting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
visuomotor training is an effective way to promote letter learning in early years, and that it should be considered as a complementary teaching strategy to visual teaching.
teaching letters with the whole body is more effective than teaching them with only the eyes.
visuomotor interventions may have a beneficial effect on letter learning in kindergarten.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way in which we teach children letters matters.
the visuomotion of letters may have a greater impact on the visual perception of letter shapes, compared with visual training.
the whole-body exploration of letters may be a promising approach for the teaching of letter knowledge.
